title: I wanted to share two ideas)
body:
Hello!

I’ve been using DayStamp for a while and really appreciate its clean design and calm, non-judgmental approach to habit tracking. The app feels very intentional and well thought out.

I wanted to share two ideas that I believe could significantly improve the clarity of the calendar view, while staying fully aligned with DayStamp’s philosophy.

1) Clear distinction between skipped days and failed days

Right now, days without completion are shown in a more neutral or muted style, which looks clean visually. However, as a user, I often miss a clear distinction between two very different situations:

– days when I intentionally skipped a habit (for example, rest days or planned breaks)

– days when I planned to do the habit but failed to complete it

These two cases feel psychologically very different, but visually they look almost the same.

It would be extremely helpful to have an explicit visual marker – for example, a small cross (×) or another subtle symbol – to indicate days where the habit was actively missed, while leaving intentionally skipped days visually neutral.

This would allow the calendar to show:
– completed days
– consciously skipped days
– failed days

without adding negativity or pressure, just more semantic clarity.

2) Clearer overview of consistency through streak grouping

Additionally, it would be very useful to have an optional summary that groups consecutive completion streaks automatically and shows their lengths.

For example:
Dec 1-4 – 4 days
Dec 9-13 – 5 days

Seeing multiple streaks listed like this makes it much easier to understand where consistency was strongest and how habits evolve over time, without manually counting days on the calendar.

I believe these features would make progress tracking more transparent and insightful, while keeping the calm and respectful tone that makes DayStamp special.

Thank you for creating such a thoughtful app. I really enjoy using it.

title: Please
body: Add the ability to make a history of your actions not only for the last year, but also for the early period: there is an ability to see past years, but there is no way to make changes, even in premium.
